 ▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄ ┃
  ❯ Explain in five short paragraphs why terminal user interfaces are hard to test.                                       18:23   ┃
 ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀ ┃
 ● Terminal UIs are hard to test because what users see is not plain text; it is a stream of cursor moves, color codes, and       ┃
   partial redraws. Small rendering differences can make snapshots fail even when behavior is correct.                            ┃
                                                                                                                                  ┃
   They are also highly timing-sensitive. Input events, background tasks, and screen refreshes can race each other, so tests may  ┃
   pass locally and fail in CI due to slight speed differences.                                                                   ┃
                                                                                                                                  ┃
   Many TUIs are stateful and modal, which increases test complexity. A single key can mean different things depending on focus,  ┃
   selection, scroll position, or active pane, so test setup must reproduce exact state before each assertion.                    ┃
                                                                                                                                  ┃
   Environment differences make results unstable too. Terminal size, font/Unicode support, shell settings, OS behavior, and even  ┃
   TERM capabilities can change layout and interaction paths in ways that are hard to normalize.                                  ┃
                                                                                                                                  ┃
   Finally, asserting correctness is tricky because user intent is often semantic, not textual. You usually need to verify        ┃
   interaction flow, focus movement, and side effects, not just final output, which requires heavier harnesses than typical unit  ┃
   tests.                                                                                                                         ┃
                                                                                                                                  ┃
